title: Match slot counting and coin wallet on Redis
name: Match slot manager

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps the per-match player count correct when many players join and leave at the same time? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
join() increments the counter first and only then compares the result with the maximum, instead of reading the count and then incrementing. What does this ordering achieve?
choices: Each concurrent joiner receives a distinct value from INCR, so the capacity decision is made on a number no other joiner can share.
It lets the roster set be skipped, since the counter alone identifies the players.
It guarantees that the counter never exceeds the maximum, even briefly.
It makes the expire calls unnecessary because INCR creates the key with a TTL.

questions.prompt: In claim_daily_bonus(), the process crashes right after the SET NX succeeds but before HINCRBY runs. What is the outcome for that player?
choices: The next call credits the bonus, because the missing coins are detected.
The claim marker expires immediately because the write was incomplete.
The player cannot claim again for the rest of the window and never receives the coins.
Redis rolls the SET back when the client connection drops.

questions.prompt: spend() runs the balance check and deduction inside a Lua script rather than calling HGET and then HINCRBY from Python. What is the practical effect?
choices: Concurrent spends are serialized by Python's GIL, so two spends cannot overlap.
Redis runs the script as one uninterrupted unit, so no other command can change the balance between the check and the deduction.
The script retries automatically when the balance changes underneath it.
The coins hash is locked against reads while the script runs, so balance() blocks.
